_doc: Per-app rule weightings. One review harness, three different problems --
reso-landing-app (Next 14, purchased template) is largely a marketing-aesthetics
problem; reso-management-app (Next 16, React 19, Tailwind 4) is mostly
design-system conformance, where the deterministic layer does nearly all the
work; reso-web-app (Next 13) sits between.
WEIGHT SEMANTICS, and the one direction a weight may not move:
0.0        SUPPRESSED. The rule does not appear in this app's report at all.
Reserved for rules whose findings are structurally unactionable
there -- token drift inside a template nobody on the team authored
is a true statement and a dead letter, and a re-reported true
finding spends the same credibility as a wrong one.
0 < w < 1  DEMOTED. Reported, one severity rung down, ordered below full-weight
findings.
1.0        Reported at the severity the rule itself assigned.
A weight may LOWER a severity and may never RAISE one. The rule that measured the
defect stays the authority on how bad it is; a profile only says how much this app
intends to act on it. Without that asymmetry a weighting file becomes a second,
un-measured severity model competing with the first.
tokens_authoritative=false demotes token conformance from an assertion to an
ABSTENTION, so it routes to the judge instead of failing. This is not a
preference: PIPELINE_SPEC 1.0 rules that token conformance must abstain rather
than FAIL wherever the winning declaration came from a token-map-less engine, and
Tailwind 4 ships no token map. Engaged mechanically whenever a profile declares
it, so an app with no palette to conform to cannot be reported as non-conformant.
gestalt is the one blind whole-frame model call per page. It is advisory triage,
never a gate -- the June 2026 campaign ratified taste-stays-human, and nothing in
this file may promote a judgement finding into a pass/fail.

default.problem: unweighted -- every rule at the severity it assigned itself

why: Next 14, purchased template. The team did not author its design system and will
not refactor it, so conformance findings against it are unactionable by
construction. What actually decides this app is whether the first second of
attention lands where the page intends -- which is the one thing no rule here
can measure and the blind gestalt call can.
Next 16, React 19, Tailwind 4 -- an app the team owns end to end, where a token
or grid deviation is a real bug with a real edit site. The deterministic layer
does nearly all the work here, so the model's share is small and stays advisory.
Tailwind 4 ships no token map, so colour/radius conformance abstains rather than
asserting a violation against a palette it cannot see.
